The [Schema Markup Generator](/schema-markup-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Generate JSON-LD schema markup — Article, FAQ, Product, Organization. Enter your schema type and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Generate JSON-LD schema markup — the structured data search engines read — for an Article, an FAQ page, a Product or an Organization. Fill in the fields and copy the finished <script type="application/ld+json"> block into your page. Schema markup is what powers rich results: FAQ drop-downs, product prices and article details in search results. Everything runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Schema Markup Generator

Start by choosing your schema type from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Pick the schema type that matches your page.
2. Fill in the fields — only the required ones are mandatory.
3. Copy the generated JSON-LD and paste it into your page's <head>.

## How it works

The [Schema Markup Generator](/schema-markup-generator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

Here is a typical example. An Article with a headline, author and date produces a JSON-LD block with @type Article and those fields — paste it into the page's <head>. Try the same figures in the [Schema Markup Generator](/schema-markup-generator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. ## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Schema Markup Generator](/schema-markup-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What schema markup does

It describes a page's content in a machine-readable format (schema.org vocabulary, written as JSON-LD). Search engines use it to understand what a page is — an article with an author and date, a product with a price, a page of questions and answers — and may show that information as a rich result. It does not guarantee a rich result, and it must describe content that is actually on the page.

## Which type to use

Article for blog posts and news; FAQPage for pages that list questions and answers (each question needs a visible answer on the page); Product for pages that sell something, with a price and currency; Organization for a company's home page, with its name, URL and logo.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Only mark up content that is visible on the page — hidden markup can get a manual penalty.
- Test the result in Google's Rich Results Test before publishing.
- FAQ markup needs at least one question and answer pair.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is schema markup?

Structured data in JSON-LD format that describes a page's content to search engines — an article's headline and author, a product's price, a list of questions and answers. Try it with your own numbers in the [Schema Markup Generator](/schema-markup-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does schema markup improve rankings?

Not directly. It can earn rich results (FAQ drop-downs, prices, ratings) in search results, which can raise click-through rates. Try it with your own numbers in the [Schema Markup Generator](/schema-markup-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Where does the JSON-LD go?

Inside a <script type="application/ld+json"> block in the page's <head> (or anywhere in the body). It is invisible to visitors. Try it with your own numbers in the [Schema Markup Generator](/schema-markup-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Schema Markup Generator?

Just Schema type. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
